_note: ⛔ SNG-403. LOCAL LAYOUTS. Erik: 'the docks in millbrook on the river, the smithy, the fields.' ⚠️ THE TERRAIN GENERATOR HAS NOTHING AT THIS SCALE — its finest feature is ~0.3° ≈ 33 km and a village spans ~0.01° ≈ 1 km. That is the pattern the detailing engine should learn.
_frame: `localMap: {bearing, metres}` from the settlement centre. Bearing 0 = toward the pole (up-map), 90 = east. ⚠️ METRES, not degrees — a village is 400-800 m across and degrees at that scale are unreadable. The engine converts: dLat = metres·cos(bearing)/111320, dLon = metres·sin(bearing)/(111320·cos(lat)).
_derivation: ⛔ THE THREE GRADIENTS THE WORLD ALREADY KNOWS, measured at each settlement: (1) RIVER BEARING and distance — from the traced hydrology; (2) UPHILL BEARING — sample the generator's raw elevation around the point; (3) ROAD BEARINGS — from connections' worldPos. ⚠️ Water trades go riverward. Terraces and orchards go uphill. Fields take the flat. Gates and markets sit on the road bearings. Everything else fills the middle.

_basisNote: ⛔ SNG-404 §2 asked CCode to tune the relief threshold against these eight layouts. ⚠️ MY OWN DATA COULD NOT ANSWER IT AND I HAD TO FIX THE DATA FIRST. I recorded intent in PROSE (`why`) and nothing machine-readable, so 'did this site use the uphill gradient?' could only be guessed by comparing bearings — and that guess is wrong: Greywater's skiff landing sits at bearing 85 against a noise-uphill of 90, so it READS as uphill-placed when it was placed on the ROAD. ⛔ AT RELIEF 0.002 THE UPHILL BEARING IS NOISE, AND NOISE COINCIDES WITH THINGS. `basis` now states which gradient decided each placement: river | uphill | anti-uphill | road | anti-road | between | prose | tradition | inferred. THE THRESHOLD IS TUNABLE FROM THIS FIELD, not from bearing arithmetic.
_thresholdFinding:
⛔ SNG-417. THE RELIEF THRESHOLD IS NOW ≈ 0.08, AND IT ONLY APPLIES WHEN THE PROSE IS SILENT.
On EIGHT towns I could only say it lay between 0.053 and 0.541 and refused to narrow it on three points. ⚠️ TWELVE TOWNS SPLIT THE CLASSES CLEANLY once prose-driven placements are separated from gradient-driven ones:
   PROSE names a slope → uphill used regardless of relief: millbrook 0.015 ('terraced gardens CLIMB THE LOWER SLOPES'), echo river crossing 0.017 ('granite shoulders').
   PROSE SILENT, uphill USED:     0.104, 0.346, 0.541, 0.567
   PROSE SILENT, uphill NOT used: 0.001, 0.002, 0.010, 0.018, 0.050, 0.053
⛔ BOUNDARY BETWEEN 0.053 AND 0.104. THRESHOLD 0.08. The bracket narrowed 9.6× by doubling the corpus, which is what a corpus is for.
⚠️ AND THE HARDEST CASE CONFIRMS THE ORDER: harmonic_heights_terrace measures 0.001 — the flattest reading here — AND IT IS A TERRACE ON A HEIGHTS. The world layer is measuring the valley floor the terrace meets; the terrace is below the generator's floor. No measurement at that location can find its slope, and only the seed knows: 'the LOWEST TERRACE, where the sonic civilization meets the valley floor.' ⛔ PROSE FIRST IS NOT A TIEBREAK. IT IS THE PRIMARY SOURCE.
_towardNote: ⛔ SNG-404 §5. `toward` NAMES WHICH ROAD. CCode: 'road is 14 of your 33 placements and cannot be placed without knowing WHICH road.' He is right — a bearing alone is only meaningful while the destination stands still, and SNG-407 moved eleven locations. ⚠️ `relation`: `on` = astride the way (11 of 15, exact to 0°) · `near` = beside it but set back (Mara Wells' store 18° off, the survey camp 24° off — both deliberately not IN the traffic) · `away` = placed by its ABSENCE. ⛔ THE `away` CASE IS THE ONE THAT PROVES THE FIELD IS NEEDED: Greywater's Deep Platforms sit at 178° from the Echo River Crossing road — 'whoever needed somewhere the aligned powers don't reach'. A bare bearing cannot say 'as far from that road as the town allows'; a named road with `away` can, and it STAYS TRUE IF THE ROAD MOVES.
_driftAudit: ⛔ RE-MEASURED AFTER SNG-407. Four of eight towns had a river bearing drift past 25° — Echo River Crossing 68°, Greyhearth 84°, Kindlerow 92°, the Figure-Works 87°. ⚠️ BUT ONLY 1 OF 38 PLACEMENTS ACTUALLY MOVED, because `basis` says which gradient each one used: 14 are `road` and roads move WITH the town, 5 are `prose`, 3 `tradition`, 3 `between`. Only the `river` and `uphill` ones were exposed. ⛔ THAT IS THE FIELD EARNING ITSELF. Without `basis` I would have had to re-derive all 38 by hand or leave all 38 suspect; with it the audit was five placements and a measurement.

sites.name: The Churn Road
sites.why: ⚠️ The third road, to Unspooling — the way out that is neither side, which some people take.

sites.name: The Root Gate
sites.why: ⛔ The way IN to the grown city. Not a wall's gate — where the tended wood begins to be a street.

sites.why: ⛔ 'Patient in a way that reads as either profound hospitality or a very slow trap.' Where outsiders wait, on the road out, and both readings are available to them while they do.

sites.why: ⚠️ The only road out that matters, and it goes to the town that has to live with both poles.

sites.why: ⛔ 'Streets are PAVED with light-guides; at dusk the whole district glows FROM BELOW.' The streets are the infrastructure — they are not lit, they are the light.

sites.why: ⚠️ 'Photonic-crystal towers catch and BRAID the sunlight into working beams.' Level 2 — they must be above the streets to catch anything.

sites.name: The Low Lamp Inn
sites.why: ⛔ ALREADY CANON FROM PLAY, and its own seed places it: 'tucked into the LOWER TIER of the Edge District where the light-guides run dim.' ⚠️ LEVEL −1 — the one place here that is deliberately below the light. That is why people drink in it.

sites.name: The Dim Quarter
sites.why: Where the light-guides run dim generally. ⛔ A city of light needs somewhere unlit, and it will be the lower tier every time.

sites.name: The Valley Road
sites.why: Down to the valley floor. ⚠️ The contamination teams go out this way toward the Echo.

⛔ THIS IS THE TEST CASE. It is `tier: site`, parent `the_cogitarium`, and it is STACKED at 0.00° with both the Cogitarium and the third terrace. It has NO connections of its own, so `roadsOut` is empty — the same shape as the Crossing.
⚠️ SO A LOCAL LAYOUT FOR A SITE IS REALLY A LAYOUT INSIDE A BUILDING, AND ITS FRAME IS ITS PARENT'S. I have authored it at a 60 m radius with levels, and its bearings are measured FROM THE HALL, not from the Cogitarium.
⛔ THE QUESTION FOR CCODE: does `localMap` nest, so a site's sites resolve inside the site's frame? If yes this is correct as authored. If the frame must always be the settlement, these three rooms need re-expressing from the Cogitarium's centre and the metres get larger.

sites.name: The Terrace Stair

sites.name: The Lower Bend

sites.name: The Upper Bend

sites.name: The High Pass
sites.why: ⛔ THE TOP, AND THE WAY OUT OF THE VALE. Erik: 'a way out of the Valley, connecting to other parts of the world.' Level 2 — everything else here is below it.

sites.name: The Roost Fork
sites.why: ⚠️ Where the Roost trail leaves the switchback. 'Travelers between the Roost, the wilds, and the pass' — three ways, and this is where two of them part.

sites.why: ⛔ 'CLEARINGS THAT SEEM ARRANGED.' The central one, and the word is 'seem' — nobody will say by whom.

sites.why: ⚠️ 'Old trees grown STRANGE AND DELIBERATE.' Placed uphill because that is where you notice the arrangement — you look up the slope and the spacing is wrong.

sites.name: The Warden Edge
sites.why: ⛔ 'The few who live AT ITS EDGE call themselves wardens and won't say more.' At the edge, on the road in — they meet you before you are inside.

sites.name: The Watching Ground
sites.why: ⚠️ 'Animals that watch TOO KNOWINGLY.' Away from every road — the part of the grove nobody has a reason to cross, which is where you notice being watched.

sites.name: The Deepwood Path
sites.why: ⛔ Toward the Ents. 'Something tends this place' — and the Ents are three days that way, which the wardens do not comment on either.
